evals.name: order-service-fact-check
evals.prompt: Before I send docs/order-service-design.md to review, fact-check it. Check its claims against the code in src/ and the load-test data in perf/. Write an accuracy report to accuracy-report.md. Do not edit the design doc. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill makes the reviewer extract every verifiable claim, refuse the document's own word as evidence, classify each claim with a fixed taxonomy and severity, and pair each wrong claim with a correction and source. Without it, reviews tend to spot-check the obvious claims, accept 'AWS recommends' and 'well known' assertions, and skip verified claims or corrections.
expectations: Refutes the 10,000 RPS claim with the measured ceiling from perf/results.csv

Contradicted implementation and data claims are caught with file evidence: all four are classified as wrong (Inaccurate or INCORRECT) with the file that contradicts them: 10k RPS (perf/results.csv peaks near 2,310), retry (src/retry.js is a single try), auth (src/auth.js decodes without signature check), parameterized SQL (orderRepo.search concatenates input)

Catches the less obvious evidence: Notes at least one of: notifyBilling in src/client.js bypasses withRetry (so 'every outbound call' is false even if retry existed), or the 10,000 target run had a 48% error rate and 9.1 s p99

Approach and authority claims are not taken on trust: the 'AWS recommends / well known exactly-once' claim is classified unverified or wrong (outbox plus stream is at-least-once) and needs a docs citation; the one-sprint rollout is Overstated because the 'already built' parts are not built
True claims stay verified: 400 KB DynamoDB item limit and 15-minute Lambda limit are classified Verified/CONFIRMED, not listed as problems

Report follows the skill's structure: Summary with total and per-class counts using a fixed five-class taxonomy, findings grouped by severity, and original text + corrected text + source for each wrong or overstated claim. Either the Verified/Inaccurate/Overstated/Unverifiable/Missing Context names or the CONFIRMED/INCORRECT/OVERSTATED/UNVERIFIED/MISSING CONTEXT names count.
Report gives an explicit overall verdict on whether the doc is ready for review (for example PASS/FAIL or ready/not ready) that follows from the blocking findings

AWS limit claims (400 KB DynamoDB item, 15-minute Lambda timeout) cite a named AWS primary source (a docs.aws.amazon.com page or the AWS service quotas/limits documentation), or the report states plainly that they were checked from memory without live AWS docs

scripted_checks.text: Refutes the 10,000 RPS claim with the measured ceiling from perf/results.csv

evals.name: export-feasibility
evals.prompt: Our design review is Thursday. Check whether docs/export-design.md will actually work as written, using the code in src/ and the timings in perf/. Write your findings to export-accuracy.md. Do not edit the design doc. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: Step 4 of the skill traces the execution path end to end and flags any step that assumes an unconfirmed capability; its guidelines say service limits must be checked against current documentation. Without it, a reviewer tends to check the individual sentences and miss that a synchronous API Gateway plus Lambda request cannot return a 1.2 GB file or run for minutes.
expectations: Finds the end-to-end feasibility break: States that the synchronous request path cannot carry a 1.2 GB response or a multi-minute run, citing the relevant limits (API Gateway REST 29 s integration timeout and 10 MB payload, Lambda 6 MB sync response) or explicitly marking them to verify in current AWS docs
The 'already streams to S3' claim is refuted from the code: marked wrong (Inaccurate or INCORRECT) citing src/exporter.js: builds the whole CSV in memory and writes to /tmp, no S3 or multipart call

Sizing and timing claims are checked against perf/export-timings.csv: Shows 40 s is only the medium-tier median (large tier p50 212 s, p95 610 s, max 1,480 s) and that /tmp defaults to 512 MB unless configured, so both claims are Overstated or Missing Context

No false positives on the true or unknowable claims: scheduler retry is acknowledged as real (3 attempts in src/scheduler.js) with the caveat that the on-demand path never calls it; rate limiting is unverifiable (Unverifiable/UNVERIFIED) rather than wrong; limits not found in the repo are not stated as certain facts without a source or hedge

Gives a usable correction and alternative: Proposes corrected text and a workable path (e.g. async job writing to S3 with a presigned download URL, Lambda ephemeral storage or streaming upload), and corrects the 'no new infrastructure, one week' plan

Each AWS service-limit claim used in the report (API Gateway timeout and payload, Lambda response size, Lambda /tmp size) names its primary source (a docs.aws.amazon.com page) or is explicitly marked as unverified against current AWS docs, and the report says how AWS claims were checked

Report states an overall PASS/FAIL or ready/not-ready result that follows from the blocking (wrong or overstated) findings, and treats the unverifiable rate-limiting claim as a non-blocking item that needs a note or callout saying what was searched, rather than as a blocker or a confirmed fact
